$comment: Metric-action rule registry. See shared/mesh_runtime/metric_action_rules.py for the full format spec. Rules are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first match wins. Put more specific rules before more general ones. Every rule carries its own bounds — the engine enforces those at match time, so a typo cannot produce a runaway actuation.

rules.name: scale on consumer lag
rules.$doc: Covers Kafka consumer lag, RabbitMQ queue depth, Celery backlog, and SQS approximate-messages metrics. A single rule fires across the four queue technologies because they all look like 'unread messages climbing'. Only triggers at ≥30% delta so transient bursts don't churn replicas.
rules.rollback_plan: scale deployment back to the prior replica count if the lag does not drop within 10 minutes

rules.name: scale on cpu saturation
rules.$doc: CPU utilization crossing 85% typically responds well to adding replicas, especially for stateless workloads. Note we match on the OTel semantic convention metric names (system.cpu.utilization, process.cpu.utilization) plus the common Prometheus-style node_cpu_seconds_total variants.
rules.rollback_plan: scale back down once CPU utilization returns below 60% for 10 minutes

rules.name: raise memory limit on saturation
rules.$doc: When memory.usage climbs toward memory.limit, the right answer is usually to raise the limit rather than scale replicas — unless the workload is actually leaking, in which case the subsequent restart still buys time. We patch limits instead of resetting the pod because Mesh already has restart_deployment for the leak case.
rules.rollback_plan: restore the previous memory limits using the captured baseline before patching

rules.name: scale on request rate spike
rules.$doc: Broad fallback for latency-adjacent metrics: request rate, concurrent connections, active sessions. Fires only at 50% delta to keep it conservative — request rate moves a lot naturally. Consumer-lag and CPU rules above will usually fire first for known workloads.
rules.rollback_plan: scale back to prior replica count once the traffic burst subsides
